Saudi Stocks Rise 0.2%, Supported by Aramco Gains
sum: Saudi stocks ended Thursday's session with modest gains amid mixed performance among heavyweight shares, as Saudi Aramco and several other companies advanced, offsetting declines in banking stocks and shares affected by third-quarter earnings.
The benchmark Tadawul All Share Index (TASI) rose 0.2% to close at 10,326 points, gaining 18 points, with total trading value reaching approximately SAR 4.1 billion ($1.09 billion).
Saudi Aramco shares climbed 1.5% to SAR 26.40, with around 12 million shares changing hands in trades worth more than SAR 300 million.
Meanwhile, Al Rajhi Bank shares declined 0.6%, while ACWA Power fell 0.5%.

United Carton Industries Company (UCIC) jumped nearly 6% after announcing a cash dividend distribution to shareholders. Shares of Al-Omran Industrial Trading, Azm and Saudi Industrial Development Company (SIDC) also rose between 5% and 8%.
On the losing side, Raoom led the decliners, falling 8% to SAR 73.90, with approximately 2.2 million shares traded for a total value of SAR 170 million.
Among stocks affected by third-quarter 2026 financial results, Saudi Arabian Refineries Company dropped 4.6%, Ladun Investment fell 3.9%, and Al Jouf Cement declined 0.7%.

Al Rajhi Bank stock: lender leads Saudi banks in nine-month profit
sum: Saudi Arabia's listed banks delivered stronger earnings through the first nine months of 2026, with Al Rajhi Bank leading the sector. Asharq Al-Awsat reported on October 27 that the ten listed Saudi banks generated combined net profit of 73.58 billion Saudi riyals in the first nine months, up 6.84 percent year over year.

Al Rajhi Bank recorded nine-month net profit of 20.87 billion Saudi riyals, an increase of 13.3 percent from the prior-year period, according to the report. Saudi National Bank ranked second at 19.48 billion Saudi riyals, while Riyad Bank followed with nearly 8.13 billion Saudi riyals.

Third-quarter profit at Al Rajhi reached 7.1 billion Saudi riyals, up 11.73 percent year over year. The report linked sector momentum to lending growth, strong credit demand and Saudi economic expansion, while analysts highlighted funding costs, liquidity, capital and nonperforming loans as risks to monitor.
Al Rajhi Bank stock traded at 63.85 Saudi riyals on Tadawul at 13:18 CET on Tuesday, November 10, 2026. The latest available quotation followed a session that closed before the publication date.

Based in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, Al Rajhi Bank focuses on Islamic banking and provides retail and broader banking services, including mortgage and consumer financing. The bank operates a large domestic network and serves Saudi customers through branches, ATMs and point-of-sale infrastructure, according to its investor relations page. Its listed Saudi competitors include Saudi National Bank and Riyad Bank; Al Rajhi held the highest nine-month profit among the group covered by Asharq Al-Awsat. The bank's scale and retail exposure make loan growth, deposit costs and asset quality central investment considerations.
Saudi banking shares remain linked to domestic credit demand and economic development activity; see Current market reports.

items.t: Mideast Stocks: Gulf stocks close higher as Trump dials back Iran strike talk
Gulf Stock Markets Rise as Trump Signals Pause in Iran Strikes
sum: Gulf stock markets opened higher on Tuesday as investors responded to US President Donald Trump’s decision to hold off on further military strikes against Iran, raising hopes of a temporary reduction in regional tensions.

Gains across Saudi Arabia, Dubai, Abu Dhabi and Qatar came as markets assessed the possibility of renewed diplomatic engagement, although the continued naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz and fresh missile attacks on Saudi territory limited the improvement in the security outlook.

Trump said military action against Iran was not needed “at this point” after regional allies, including Qatar’s prime minister, appealed for restraint. His position signaled a pause in further strikes rather than a resolution of the conflict. The US naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz remains in place, leaving a major route for global oil shipments exposed to continued disruption.

Saudi Arabia’s benchmark index rose 0.3%, supported by gains in major companies. Al Rajhi Bank advanced 1%, while ACWA Power climbed 2%. Saudi Aramco, however, fell 1.5%, indicating that the improvement in broader market sentiment did not extend to all sectors.

Dubai’s main share index performed more strongly, gaining 1.4%. Top lender Emirates NBD rose 3.6%, providing substantial support to the market. Logistics company Aramex surged 10.7%, becoming the index’s biggest gainer after reporting a sharp increase in third-quarter profit.
Abu Dhabi’s benchmark index advanced 0.5%, while Qatar’s main index gained 0.7%.

Riyad Bank stock in focus after record Q3 operating income
sum: Riyad Bank reported record quarterly operating income of SAR 5 billion in its third-quarter 2026 presentation on November 3. According to Investing.com, nine-month net income rose 5% year over year to SAR 8.1 billion, while total operating income increased 5% to SAR 14.4 billion.

Riyad Bank shares traded at 19.77 Saudi riyals on Tadawul at 13:10 CET on Sunday, November 8, 2026. The latest available quote places the stock near the lower end of its 52-week range of 18.59 to 22.41 Saudi riyals.

Operating efficiency improved as expenses before impairment rose just 1% year over year. The cost-to-income ratio fell to 28.7%, below the bank's guidance threshold of 30%, while return on equity reached 16.6% for the nine-month period.

Balance-sheet growth remained selective. Total assets increased 5% year to date to SAR 545 billion, loans grew 3% to SAR 385 billion and customer deposits declined 1% to SAR 329 billion. Management highlighted funding diversification, including a SAR 10 billion additional Tier 1 sukuk issued during the third quarter.

Management said its fiscal 2026 guidance remained on track. Net special commission income growth exceeded the mid- to high-single-digit target range, the cost-to-income ratio stayed below 30% and the cost of credit risk remained within the 35 to 45 basis-point range. Loan growth of 3.2% year to date was within the annual target range, although management indicated that full-year growth could finish toward the lower end.
The bank has not provided firm 2027 guidance, citing regional geopolitical uncertainty. Investors will therefore focus on full-year results and the next update on the Strategy 2030 execution plan.

Riyad Bank is a Saudi Arabian commercial bank headquartered in Riyadh. Its services include accounts, financing, credit cards, digital banking and rewards programs for retail customers, alongside corporate and investment banking activities. In the domestic market, it competes with larger institutions such as Saudi National Bank and Al Rajhi Bank, while Bank AlJazira is another listed Saudi banking peer; Riyad Bank occupies a sizeable but more specialized position than the two largest lenders.

items.t: BofA adds TSLA, AVGO, IBM, others to its Global Defenders list
sum: Bank of America this week added mega-cap names including Tesla TSLA, Broadcom AVGO, and IBM IBM to its quantitative Global Defenders list, updating its screen of richly priced equities that have lagged the market.

The screen identifies the 30 highest price-to-earnings stocks displaying below-average earnings momentum and price momentum, balanced across sectors and global regions. Global Defenders surged 4.0% in October, capitalized on a worldwide rotation where weak-momentum and value shares rebounded while high-flying momentum leaders retreated.

That gain allowed the cohort to beat the benchmark MSCI AC World Index (-1.7%) and outpace the Global Contenders strategy (-3.2%) by 7.2 percentage points, narrowing the Contenders' 12-month performance lead to 8.4%.
Among the other new entrants to the Global Defenders roster include Motorola MSI in the U.S., alongside Australia's Westpac WEBNF, China's Xpeng XPEV, and Norway's DNB Bank DNBBY.

items.t: Mideast Stocks: Gulf bourses advance as investors weigh US midterms and Iran standoff
sum: Gulf bourses advanced in early trade on Wednesday as investors weighed the fallout from the US midterms and waited to see how Washington would respond in its war with Iran.
Democrats seized the Senate and the House, dealing a setback to President Donald Trump. Their wins in South Carolina, Texas and Ohio broke through long-held Republican territory.
Saudi Arabia's benchmark index gained 1.7%, lifted by a 6.7% jump in Saudi Arabian Mining Company and a 1.4% rise in Al Rajhi Bank.

The US carried out "defensive" strikes on Iran's Qeshm island targeting surface-to-air missiles used against US assets, a US official said on Tuesday. Another official said the strikes appeared limited and did not signal a return to major combat operations.
In Qatar, the index leapt 2.3%, with almost all its constituents in positive territory including Qatar Islamic Bank , which was up 3.3%.
Doha announced on Tuesday that Washington and Tehran remain dedicated to mediation and are examining proposals meant to close the distance between them.
Qatari officials also reported recent progress in discussions with each side, and efforts to shrink the differences between them are still underway.

items.t: Mideast Stocks: Gulf bourses mixed as Iran-Saudi talks offset fears over US strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island
sum: Major Gulf bourses were mixed in early trade on Tuesday, as Iran's statement that talks with Saudi Arabia were continuing was offset by escalation fears in the eight-month conflict after the US struck Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz.

A US official said on Monday that the strikes, earlier reported by the Wall Street Journal, appeared limited and did not mark a resumption of major combat operations. The official spoke on the condition of anonymity.

Saudi Arabia's benchmark index slipped 0.2% in choppy trade, weighed down by a 0.4% fall in Al Rajhi Bank . Oil giant Saudi Aramco eased 0.2%, even though it reported a steep rise in third-quarter profit.

Aramco said on Tuesday that its net profit rose 34.5% despite attacks targeting the company. The increase came mainly from higher revenue and its exit from a joint venture. The US-Iran war has cut Aramco's output, but higher oil prices have offset the lower volumes.
Alongside the results, the company declared a base dividend of $21.9 billion.

With the conflict disrupting operations, Aramco is also looking at ways to protect its exports. CEO Amin Nasser told Reuters in a statement that the company is exploring additional export routes and overseas capacity, including a possible expansion of its East-West pipeline.
On the other hand, Al Majed for Oud Co soared 8.6%, a day after reporting 50% jump in third-quarter profit.

items.t: Alinma Bank stock: ANB Capital flags Q3 profit miss versus forecast
sum: Alinma Bank's third-quarter earnings remain under scrutiny after ANB Capital said net profit of SAR 1.58 billion came in 6.3% below its forecast. The assessment was reported in a November 1, 2026 note by Argaam.

The result places credit costs and the quality of income at the center of the investment case. A weaker-than-forecast quarterly outcome can raise the importance of provisioning trends, financing growth and fee income when investors assess the bank's next reporting period.

ANB Capital's assessment follows Alinma Bank's third-quarter reporting for 2026. The analyst view points to a gap between the reported quarterly profit and expectations, while leaving the broader earnings outlook dependent on how financing income develops alongside credit charges.
Alinma Bank stock traded at 21.59 Saudi riyals on the Saudi Exchange at 1:19:22 p.m. CET on Sunday, November 1, 2026.

Alinma Bank provides Shariah-compliant retail and corporate banking, asset management and brokerage services, with its main operations in Saudi Arabia. The bank is headquartered in Riyadh and serves the Kingdom's financial market. It competes with Al Rajhi Bank, Saudi National Bank and Bank Albilad; Alinma is positioned as a Saudi-focused Islamic lender with a broad banking and investment-services offering.

Saudi Arabia Consumer Lending Market to Grow at a CAGR of 2.67% (Outstanding Balance) and 2.58% (Gross Lending) During 2026-2032 | Vyansa Intelligence
sum: NEW DELHI, March 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- According to the market research report published by Vyansa Intelligence, the Consumer Lending Market in Saudi Arabia is projected to register an outstanding balance CAGR of around 2.67% and gross lending CAGR of around 2.58% during 2026-32. The market growth is primarily driven by increasing demand for housing finance, rising consumer credit penetration, and the gradual expansion of structured financial services across the Kingdom.

- The Saudi Arabia Consumer Lending Market recorded an outstanding balance of approximately USD 434.45 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach around USD 522.45 billion by 2032, reflecting steady and sustained growth. Meanwhile, gross lending stood at USD 252.49 billion in 2025 and is expected to grow to USD 301.74 billion by 2032, supported by consistent borrowing demand and financial sector expansion.

- By loan type, mortgages / home loans dominate the market with nearly 55% share, driven by increasing homeownership initiatives, government-backed housing programs, and rising residential development across Saudi Arabia.
- By distribution channel, bank branches account for approximately 75% of the market share, highlighting the continued dominance of traditional banking infrastructure in consumer lending activities.
- More than 5 companies are actively operating in the Saudi Arabia consumer lending market, indicating a moderately competitive landscape.
- The top four companies collectively hold a significant share of the market, including Saudi National Bank (SNB), Al Rajhi Bank, Riyad Bank, and Arab National Bank (ANB) Bank.
